entities.name: Barisan Nasional
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
Barisan Nasional (BN) is a political coalition in Malaysia, formally established in 1973, which has played a pivotal role in the governance of the country for several decades. Originally formed as the Alliance Party, it became a coalition of various political parties, primarily representing the interests of the Malay majority, Chinese, and Indian communities in Malaysia. Headquartered in Kuala Lumpur, BN has been instrumental in shaping Malaysia's political landscape, particularly during its formative years post-independence, when it contributed to the establishment of a stable government amidst ethnic diversity and communal tensions.

The coalition first came to prominence during the 1974 general elections, where it secured a significant majority in the Parliament, allowing it to implement policies aimed at national development and unity. Under the leadership of notable figures such as Tun Abdul Razak and later Tun Dr. Mahathir Mohamad, BN pursued a platform of economic growth, infrastructure development, and social stability. It championed the New Economic Policy (NEP) in 1971, which aimed to eradicate poverty and restructure societal imbalances, fundamentally altering the socio-economic fabric of Malaysia.

Barisan Nasional's grip on power began to wane in the 21st century, culminating in its historic defeat in the 2018 general elections, which marked a significant political shift in Malaysia. This defeat not only ended BN's 61-year reign but also paved the way for the rise of the Pakatan Harapan coalition, demonstrating the electorate's demand for reform and accountability. The legacy of BN can be seen in the continuing discourse surrounding race relations and governance, as well as in the evolving political dynamics in Malaysia.
